name: dmlab_explore_goal_locations_small
title: DMLab explore_goal_locations_small
note: This manifest is the explore_goal_locations_small bundle AND the family pins (reference): tools/bundle_multifile.py --all reads every */*/manifest.json, so the family file must be a real bundle manifest. Other levels: manifest_<level>.json in this directory.

obs.frame: 64x64 first-person view, 90 degree FOV, eye 0.5 cells above the floor

max_steps_source: explore factory episodeLengthSeconds default 90 s x 60 fps / action repeat 4

human.controls: W/S forward and back, A/D strafe, arrow keys or the mouse (click the view; Esc gives it back) to turn. One step is 4 engine frames at 60 fps.
human.hint: Click the view to look around with the mouse (Esc gives it back).

reference.name: DeepMind Lab (DMLab-30)

oracle.recipe: https://gist.github.com/danijar/ca6ab917188d2e081a8253b3ca5c36d3 (install-dmlab.sh, Ubuntu 22.04); reference/oracle/python_system.bzl is that gist's build glue
oracle.bazel: 7.4.1 (USE_BAZEL_VERSION); WORKSPACE deps pinned to 2023-01-04 commits by reference/oracle/pin_deps.sh

explore_goal_locations_small.host: Apple M4 Pro, Docker linux/amd64 (emulated), 1 env, 64x64 software renderer, repeat 4

action_set.note: PLAN.md section 2 listed a different order (look_left first); the scalable_agent order above is authoritative and is the action index order of the port.

constants.eye_source: DEBUG.PLAYERS.EYE.POS z at rest, all 32 seeds of explore_goal_locations_small
constants.look_source: 0.022 x 4.8 (Q3 m_yaw x sensitivity); with a per-trajectory quantisation phase the yaw is exact on every frame of all 64 trajectories (G3)

pmove.fit: explore family, 8 levels x 32 seeds x 2 trajectories x 300 frames; accel/friction grid 8/10/12 x 5/6/8 selects 10/6 sharply; wall geometry from oracle contact positions (no fitted cut)
pmove.residual: G3: 512/512 trajectories within 2.0 units every frame, yaw within 1e-3 deg, cells and rewards identical
pmove.wall_cell_collision: a cross of two boxes each inset 1 unit on one axis: a 1x1 square notch at every convex corner (oracle sits 0.874-0.875 inside both faces there; seed 22 held with zero velocity)
pmove.doors: closed: zero-thickness panel across the cell centre (H blocks y, I blocks x); open: slid +94 along its angle (H +x, I +y). Oracle stop positions.

touch_box.tested_on: frame end position; reward next frame; teleport the frame after

constants.respawn: hold h frames (0..2), then queued commands: first for M ms (17..200), rest 16 ms; fitted per event for G3 (games/<level>.replay.json); play default h=0, M=17
constants.sky_rgb: 0x89D7FF (modal top row of the oracle frames)
constants.max_steps_source: episodeLengthSeconds from each level script (else explore factory default 90) x 60 fps / action repeat 4

skymaze.platform_top: 800 - 20 x (letter - 'a'); '.' a void cell (an invisible column all the way up)
skymaze.player_box: +-15 across, -24..+32 about the origin; stands at top + 24.125
skymaze.air_move: 3D step-slide against cell columns: slide with gravity 800; if touched, the same move from 18 higher then pushed down 18 (oracle steps up 6-15 onto a ledge mid-fall, and falls past an edge its first slide clipped)
skymaze.trace: entry fraction clamped to 0, ties to the first brush side (-x, +x, -y, +y, +z); a plane is missed when d1 > 0 and d2 >= 0.125
skymaze.landing: ground within 0.25 below at a frame end; a fall that did not touch keeps |v| with its vertical speed in the next walk (friction scales vz too)
skymaze.land_hold: after a landing faster than 200 u/s down, walls stop the box but leave the velocity unclipped for 250 ms
skymaze.msec: falling frames from the vertical speed (gravity 11 vs 14 u/s); ground frames from the friction+accel velocity update when only one of 14/17 reproduces it
skymaze.residual: G3: 128/128 trajectories within 2.0 units every frame, yaw within 1e-3 deg, cells and rewards identical

watermaze.map: em_watermaze: 16 wedge-shaped wall brushes (non-axial planes, collided as they are, behind Quake's axial bevels), floor at 0, solid translucent glass (map/water_d) at 16: the player stands at 40.125
watermaze.platform: random within radius 580 of the centre (factory); its button an octagon 64 across the flats; the player's box touching it (frame end) arms it
watermaze.hold: 6 frames after arming, the player is put on the platform centre at rest and held (the oracle re-centres every 6 frames); its height then follows the measured rise to 118.125
watermaze.reward: +1 at 10 frames into the hold, then every 1000 ms of engine time; one period after the 5th the map restarts at a spawn point
watermaze.probe: reference/oracle/probe_watermaze.py: a walk-on and a 3-unit creep give the same hold/reward/rise frames; arming-to-hold is 6 or 7 frames (server tick phase): the port uses 6
watermaze.spawn_fall: the spawn at z 64 is still falling when the episode starts (vz from the first frame: -199)
watermaze.render: walls as their own 16 faces and the 8 landmarks (MD3 picture frames, modelscale 0.5, front view) as flat pictures 12.5 units off the wall, both rs_maze_quads; the glass as an opaque composite over the floor: a G6 approximation
watermaze.residual: G3: 64/64 trajectories within 2.0 units every frame, yaw within 1e-3 deg, cells and rewards identical (no dump trajectory reaches the platform)

read: game_scripts/language/{make,constraints,object_generator,item_count,placers,reward_controllers,texter}.lua (T5: the execute task rules, read as spec)
reference.parity: G2 layouts exact; G3 trajectories under the dumps' scripted actions within PLAN.md section 4 tolerances, with the oracle's engine timing, yaw phase and respawn poses as replay inputs (games/<level>.replay.json)
not_matched: pixels: no lightmaps, one static frame of each animated Q3 shader, no HUD, flat sky colour (G6 measures it)
engine timing in play: a fixed 17,17,14 ms cycle; DMLab's client-clock jitter is reproduced only in G3 replays
goal pickup: a static billboard; DMLab's model spins and bobs
the corpus is DMLab seeds 0..31; episode seed s plays corpus entry s mod 32
restarts in play: spawn, door states and object placements drawn with the port's PCG following the factories' rules, not DMLab's Lua RNG; hold 0 frames
closed doors are drawn as full wall cells (they collide as a panel across the cell centre)
human-recognisable objects: the two-colour patterns are this port's own drawings (DMLab's pattern images are under game_scripts/, GPL-2)
